indication: Adults with dMMR/MSI-H Stage II/III locally advanced rectal cancer (accelerated approval)
headline: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Jemperli as the first immunotherapy for adults with mismatch repair deficient or microsatellite instability high locally advanced rectal cancer, on the single-arm AZUR-1 study. GSK says eligible patients may be able to avoid chemotherapy, radiation and surgery; continued approval may depend on a confirmatory trial.
pdufa_note: The FDA's notification states that on October 19, 2026 it granted accelerated approval to dostarlimab (Jemperli, GSK) for adults with Stage II/III locally advanced rectal cancer that is MSI-H or dMMR (FDA, October 19, 2026). GSK announced the approval the same day from Philadelphia (GSK's announcement). The goal date was stated by GSK as February 2027 when the sBLA was accepted for priority review (GSK, August 24, 2026); because that goal is a month rather than a day, pdufa.bio publishes no early or late margin, although GSK's release says the approval came ahead of the PDUFA date under Priority Review and a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher. The FDA's letter for BLA 761174 had not been posted on Drugs@FDA when this page was published. Per the FDA, AZUR-1 (NCT05723562) was a single-arm, open-label study of 154 previously untreated patients given dostarlimab 500 mg every three weeks for nine cycles; sustained clinical complete response at 12 months was 47% (95% CI 27 to 56) by independent central review in 116 evaluable patients and 68% (95% CI 60 to 76) by investigator assessment in 144, overall response by central review was 79%, and with a median follow-up of 26.3 months no patient with a complete or near-complete response had progressed. Jemperli holds Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations for this indication.
h1: Jemperli (dostarlimab) FDA accelerated approval for locally advanced rectal cancer: Oct 19, 2026
